Nvidia Say Never
Nvidia’s board voted Sunday to
reinstate Jensen Huang
as CEO, the company announced yesterday, days after foreclosing the possibility. President Donald Trump took credit for facilitating the board's reversal; Nvidia’s stock closed up 31.5% on the news, with the Nasdaq closing up 6.5%. The S&P 500 and Dow rose 4.7% and 3%, respectively, after ending in correction territory last week.
The decision was unanimous by the company’s 10-member board of directors (
who are they?
). Trump said he shared assurances with the board that there was no evidence Huang had engaged in illegal conduct. The update comes weeks after reports emerged of Huang’s relationship with an alleged Chinese spy (Huang also reportedly had affairs with
two Nvidia employees
). The New York Times on Sunday reported that the alleged spy was in contact
with China’s top spy agency
amid the affair.
In addition to an internal company probe, Huang is subject to multiple congressional investigations. He is due to testify before
three House committees
next week.
Cartel Leader Captured
The US has
requested the extradition
of alleged cartel leader Fausto Isidro Meza Flores, Mexico confirmed yesterday. His Friday arrest sparked violence across the northwestern state of Sinaloa over the weekend, leaving 16 suspected cartel members and four soldiers dead.
Meza Flores, known as “El Chapo Isidro,”
is one of the
FBI’s 10 most wanted fugitives
. The 44-year-old’s drug-trafficking history
spanned more than 20 years
. He most recently led Los Mazatlecos, a criminal organization accused of murder, torture, kidnapping, and extortion. Mexican security officials confirmed a US surveillance drone assisted in Meza Flores’ arrest (
watch video clips
). Organized crime groups control an estimated one-third of Mexico’s territory, but analysts do not expect the arrest to significantly impact the drug trade because rival organizations may expand to take over smuggling routes.
US Customs and Border Protection seized roughly 253,000 pounds of drugs from the southwest border in the 2026 fiscal year, over 57% of which was methamphetamine. See seizure statistics graphs
here

Ukrainian Attack in Libya
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy yesterday claimed credit for a drone attack on two Russian ships at a
naval base in Libya
(w/map), more than 1,500 miles from the front lines of the Russia-Ukraine war.
Kyiv has regularly targeted Moscow's military and shadow fleet, though attacks have largely been concentrated in the nearby Black and Azov seas (
see map
). Zelenskyy said the operation in Libya involved seven domestically produced naval drones launched from an undisclosed location. The attack adds to indications Ukraine may have built an extensive intelligence network in the Mediterranean; reports emerged earlier this year that Ukraine is operating in western Libya under a
covert deal
backed by Western nations. The North African nation has been divided between two rival regimes since 2014: a UN-recognized government in the west and a de facto military administration with close ties to Moscow in the east (
read background
Separately, NATO has
agreed to deploy
an early warning aircraft to Poland after three Russian missiles landed in the country Friday.
